notes: Not hooked. It stays mapped because it cannot stand in for the original inside the game yet: (1) the two statics' destructors are registered with the game CRT's atexit (table in the game CRT) and ours would register them with our own CRT, whose list the game CRT's exit never runs, so the framework and application destructors would not run at exit; (2) the statics' guard words get the game CRT's epoch number in the original and 1 in ours (nothing reads it; the test normalises it); (3) the Steam-failure path ends with the game CRT's _exit, ours calls ours; (4) the test compares the pieces behind the seams (framework constructor, application constructor, RunApp: each verified on its own; crash reporter start, analytics and handler installer: replaced by contract) as recorders, not their effects. 0x4dc940 does not block: it is a 5-byte shared_vf (never hooked) whose one store (clear the byte at +0x10 of the memory-tracking object at 0x10fda2c) WinMainBody does inline. Contracts: docs/contracts/. E1 (lane GC, docs/subsystems/startup.md 'E1: taking over the process start'): (1) and (3) are now bindings: WinMainSeams::registerAtExit and WinMainSeams::exit (renamed from exitProcess; the original's Steam-failure path calls exit 0x82f6bf, which runs the atexit list, not _exit: the old default _exit was wrong, the default is now std::exit) are bound by the host to the image CRT's atexit 0x824cbe and exit 0x82f6bf under [Startup] OwnStart=2, where the host's start sequencer (winmainstart::RunImageStart, tests/winmain_start.cpp) calls WinMainBody instead of the image's entry; (2) stays (nobody else reads the guards: xrefs of 0x10fdce8 / 0x10fdf58 are WinMain's only). In effect through its callers (2026-10-18, coordinator): the trap arms under the switch values above; in-game runs e-menu-1 / e-menu-2 (own-start-menu, exit code 0, no trap line) and e-menu-0 (OwnStart=0 unchanged).

name: RunApp(framework, app, cmdline): RunFramework directly, or inside an SEH __try when the reporter's flag byte is set
notes: Hooked (WinMain_RunApp), not run in-game. Flag byte clear: RunFramework; set: RunFrameworkGuarded in an SEH __try whose filter calls Report(app+0x98, info) for the first exception only (a second exception raised inside Report skips the report) and always selects the handler, ExitProcess(0). Returns g_ExitCode. 0x418be0 is just lea eax,[ecx+0x98]. The crash path's unwind (lane GH; the old hold, 'SEH3 vs SEH4', was fixed by the /GS- build of c943df9): ours is __SEH_prolog + _except_handler3 from our MSVC 14.40 toolchain, the same library code the original runs (0x824dc0, 0x826a30, CallDestructExceptionObject 0x829a19, _global_unwind2 0x829a60, _local_unwind2 0x829ae0: library matches), so when the filter selects the handler both destroy a thrown C++ object, then RtlUnwind with no record (STATUS_UNWIND): /EHs destructors below RunApp do not run, __finally blocks do, then ExitProcess(0). Only __ValidateEH3RN 0x829c90 is the image's own (893 B, not library-matched): it checks the frame's scope table lies in an image, which ours (in the host exe) passes; the test redirects the original's to 'valid' (the harness maps without the module data). The SEH3 frame depends on /GS-: with /GS (e.g. the TS2_ESPCHECK build) it is SEH4, whose unwind passes the record and runs the destructors, and WinMain_RunApp fails. Test (tests/winmain_run_app.cpp, nothing normalised): 390 scenarios, flag 0,1,2,0x80,0xff x framework paths x six exceptions (cError, D3D, std::runtime_error, a C++ object whose destructor logs, access violation, custom SEH code) at two places (through a C++ guard; through a C++ guard and a __finally) x Report returning, raising an SEH code or throwing C++; compares globals, refcounts, outcome (exit/exception), the full call log with every destructor and __finally, and the record Report sees (code, flags, parameters, address, context); fails unless 10 paths are reached (incl. the thrown object destroyed before ExitProcess, __finally run with no C++ destructor in the crash unwind, nested SEH and C++ from the reporter). Test fixtures: the original's Report (0x1bd69a) and the validator are redirected; ours calls Report through winmain::sRunAppReportOverride (null in the game: appbase::Report, verified). Mutants killed (GH): WinMain.size.cpp built with /GS (SEH4: ours then runs ~FrameGuard and releases the face), nested exception reported again, nested exception not handled here, ExitProcess code, Guarded/plain swapped, Report offset; earlier: counter test (3 variants), flag inverted, return value. Equivalent survivor: removing the __debugbreak after ExitProcess (unreachable). No original calls.
